# Captions and translation

## Architecture rules

- **Captions** ([details](../../docs/project/tech-stack.md#captions)): YouTube extraction stays behind `data/CaptionProvider.kt` (host allowlist, 8 MiB cap). The page only reads its own player's caption replies, never changes a request or sends its token out of the page, and `webPageTranscriptScript` keeps its one `fetch(`.

- **Translation** ([details](../../docs/project/tech-stack.md#translation)): Google Translate's web endpoint by default, on-device ML Kit as the switch and the fallback; never require a service key. Online-only languages never move to the device.

## Full text: docs/project/tech-stack.md, section 'Captions'

### Captions

- Caption discovery uses watch-page metadata and undocumented Innertube player fallbacks, then timed-text downloads, isolated behind `data/CaptionProvider.kt` / `YouTubeCaptionProvider.kt` (host allowlist, 8 MiB response cap). Keep that replaceable boundary, its timeout budgets and cancellation, so undocumented YouTube behaviour can change without rewriting the learning UI. The YouTube page fetches the track first (owner decision 2026-10-18, [spec](../../docs/specs/2026-10-18-page-first-full-transcript.md)): `PageFirstCaptionProvider` races the page (`PageTranscriptSource`, scripts in `YouTubeWebScripts.kt`) against that download; the first success wins. The page keeps a copy of the caption replies its own player downloads (`WEB_CAPTION_CAPTURE_SCRIPT`, a document-start script that only reads `/api/timedtext` and `/youtubei/v1/get_transcript` replies on YouTube hosts and never changes a request), so the app never re-sends the page's token; captions the player loads later still replace live subtitles. An empty track list in the player's details is no dead end: the player's captions menu and its downloads count too. As the last resort (owner decision 2026-10-18) the page opens YouTube's own transcript panel and takes its lines. With Settings → Captions & translation → Load captions with a page token (beta, owner request 2026-10-20: Automatic by default, On, Off), a page whose plain request comes back empty mints its own proof-of-origin token as YouTube's web player does (`ui/PageTokenScript.kt`; BotGuard's interpreter only from `https://www.google.com/js/th/`) and asks again with `pot`; once that worked, Automatic asks with the token first on later videos (`page_token_needed`) until a plain request works again, and On always asks with it first; the token never leaves the page and `webPageTranscriptScript` keeps its one `fetch(`.

## Full text: docs/project/tech-stack.md, section 'Translation'

### Translation

- Translation uses Google Translate's unofficial web endpoint by default (`translation/GoogleWebTranslator.kt`, owner decision 2026-10-05); Settings → Captions & translation switches to on-device ML Kit (`translation/OnDeviceTranslator.kt`). No user-provided/developer-provisioned service key is ever required; YouTube's internal client key handling is an extraction detail, not a key the user sets up. Settings → Captions & translation → Translate subtitles with is one choice, listed first in the section (owner request 2026-10-28, `SubtitleTranslator`): Google (default), AI translation (best quality: Google's lines while the AI is loading), AI only, or on this device only (no "beta" label, owner decision); only the chosen translator's settings show below it. The AI choices ([spec](../../docs/specs/2026-10-28-ai-subtitle-translation.md)) let the AI assistant's service and keys translate, with the AI assistant's model unless another is chosen (`translation/AiSubtitleTranslator.kt`: windows of sentences split into their rows plus earlier sentences as context, one translation per row in JSON); with Google while waiting, Google's lines show first and each sentence switches to the AI's as soon as the streamed reply contains it, while AI only waits for the AI (owner request 2026-10-28); Google keeps whatever the AI leaves out or fails on, and the assistant cannot change this setting. Settings → Captions & translation → AI thinking for translation (owner request 2026-11-02, [spec](../../docs/specs/2026-11-02-ai-translation-thinking.md)) is Off by default, or Low or Medium (no High: long windows would time out), shown only for Gemini and OpenAI; each level keeps its own translation cache, and the assistant may change it after the user's tap. When Google still fails after its retries (1 s, 3 s, 7 s; none for a block), that video uses YouTube's own translated captions, as LingoTube does (owner decision 2026-10-19, [spec](../../docs/specs/2026-10-19-youtube-translation-fallback.md): the page fetches the track with `tlang`, `PageTranslationSource`), and quietly translates on-device what YouTube does not cover; a top-right icon explains why (naming the Google address and status), and Google is checked again every 2 minutes and on every load. A row never waits long for Google (owner decision 2026-10-19, [spec](../../docs/specs/2026-10-19-quick-switch-when-google-is-slow.md)): after Settings → Captions & translation → Wait for Google (Automatic: 2 s on mobile data, 4 s on Wi-Fi; or 2, 4, 8 s) the video switches the same way while Google's request runs on, and goes back to Google, replacing the shown lines, once it answers; an unreachable address hands over to the next, and the address that last worked is tried first, kept across restarts in `google_addresses` preferences for translation and voice alike (owner request 2026-10-19, [spec](../../docs/specs/2026-10-19-remember-working-google-address.md)); after a failure on mobile data the next load on mobile data starts without Google and checks it as soon as a row plays. A line Google leaves blank is asked again alone at each address and, if still blank, only that line translates on-device; a reply with every line blank counts as a refusal. While a video plays, minutes 2 to 5 are translated in the background, one request every 3 s (owner decision 2026-10-09, [spec](../../docs/specs/2026-10-09-google-blank-lines-and-five-minutes-ahead.md)); the current minute is translated also while paused (owner request 2026-10-27, [spec](../../docs/specs/2026-10-27-translate-while-paused-and-fullscreen-menu.md)). See the [Google Translate spec](../../docs/specs/2026-10-05-opt-in-google-translate.md). The "Translate to" list (`TranslationLanguages`) holds ML Kit's 59 languages plus online-only ones (`onDevice = false`, owner pick 2026-11-02, [spec](../../docs/specs/2026-11-02-azerbaijani-and-online-only-languages.md)): those never move to the device; after a Google failure their rows take YouTube's translation, else ask Google again, a line Google leaves blank stays blank, and "On this device only" shows `status_translation_needs_online` instead of translating.
